findings.what: When the re-read fails, the Cancel header still shows 'Policy status: <pre-cancel status>' unmarked, next to the new marked Status field. The original symptom is still there.
findings.why: Acceptance line 3 says that when the re-read after a 201 cancel fails, the header marks the status as read before the cancel. Only the kit Status field (line 232) gets the '(read before the cancel)' label and the warn tone. The 'Policy status' id (line 234) still renders policy?.status as plain text. That id is the field that showed the stale status unmarked before this node (the Status field used to read 'not returned'), so the header still states a status as current that the API no longer holds. Even when the re-read succeeds, the header now shows the status twice. The derived reference wb-cancel/populated.html draws a single 'Policy status' field.

findings.what: The failed re-read tests (unit and e2e honest-1.spec.ts:39) check only the Status field and a match anywhere in the header. A second, unmarked copy of the stale status passes them.
findings.why: The tests can't fail on R1. headerText() matching /read before the cancel/ is satisfied by one marked field while another field shows the same stale value unmarked. A test that proves 'the header marks the status' needs to check that no header field shows the pre-cancel status without the mark.

findings.what: Sell and Cancel (CancelPolicy.tsx:232) always use the 'pass' tone. 'Pending' and 'Cancelled' get a green check here, while PolicyView's STATUS_TAGS draws them as pending and fail.
findings.why: The glyph and colour claim a pass the API didn't give, and the same API status now looks different from screen to screen. This is also the rule of three: status-to-tone mapping now appears five times (PolicyView STATUS_TAGS, Renew, Claim, Sell, Cancel), each one different, and they all change for the same reason.

findings.what: For a rejected fetch, the drawer's live region announces 'Request #N answered', and its visible tag reads 'Problem' rather than 'Failed'.
findings.why: RequestsDrawer.tsx:73 maps a failed entry to outcome 'problem', and the kit's announcement treats every non-pending outcome as answered. Assistive tech is told the API answered a request that got no response. The visible 'failed' comes only from the note. The in-node kit gap gave RequestLog a failed state, but InspectorDrawer has none. This is a kit gap, not a fix for the screen.
